description: Working local evidence-analysis JSON CLI with optional injected structured synthesis callback, constructed from an empty directory.

interfaces.success: JSON result on stdout; exit code 0
interfaces.data_or_io_failure: JSON error on stderr, no result on stdout; exit code 2

rules: Unknown or missing fields are rejected.
Question, titles, subjects, values and excerpts are nonempty strings.
Document text may be empty only if there are no claims needing anchoring.
Documents and claims are lists; empty lists are valid.
Document IDs and claim IDs are globally unique within their separate namespaces.
Evidence is a literal source excerpt containing normalized subject and value as bounded phrases.
Duplicate normalized subject/value/excerpt assertions within one document are rejected.
Duplicate JSON object keys, malformed types, nonstandard JSON numeric constants and invalid Unicode are rejected.

contract: Callback receives a deep copy, not mutable references to analysis state.
Every statement must match a retrieved normalized subject/value pair.
Every retrieved claim must be covered exactly once, with one statement per subject/value pair.
Every claim must carry its exact document/claim citation; missing, duplicate, unknown and mismatched citations fail.
Unretrieved input claims, invented assertions and omitted conflicting evidence fail.
Arbitrary prose and unknown fields are forbidden; synthesis prose is rendered locally from validated statements.
The callback may wrap an LLM supplied by the caller; no LLM integration, provider or model call is included.
Callback failures raise ValidationError; no fabricated fallback is returned.

implemented_algorithms: NFKC normalization, case folding and whitespace collapse for subject/value identity.
Question token overlap with an explicit English stopword set; score = 4 times subject overlap + 2 times value overlap + excerpt overlap.
Retrieve positive-scoring claims, then include every claim sharing a normalized subject, even zero-score conflicting alternatives.
Group by normalized subject and value; multiple values flag disagreement, one value across multiple document IDs flags agreement, otherwise single-source.
Preserve every alternative and its source citations; do not resolve by majority vote.
Retain original subject, value, document title, exact excerpt and first-occurrence half-open character offsets.
Generate evidence-linked conflict questions, single-source corroboration questions, answer-coverage caveats and synthesis actions.
Stable sorting of evidence, groups, alternatives, claims and citations gives deterministic output independent of input document/claim order.
Strict optional callback validation followed by local evidence-bound synthesis rendering.

measured_validation.fixture_status: ALL example and test evidence is explicitly synthetic. These are software execution results, not real-world product measurements.
verified_cases: Agreement, disagreement, minority evidence and within-document conflicts
Same-subject retrieval expansion retaining zero-score contradictory evidence
Exact source provenance and character spans
Unicode/case/whitespace normalization and preservation of signs, decimals and negation in grouping
Duplicate identifiers, duplicate assertions and duplicate JSON keys
Malformed schemas, unsupported lexical claims, invented excerpts and nonstandard JSON
Empty documents, empty claims, stopword-only questions and unrelated questions
Deterministic repeated output, reordered input and byte-identical CLI output
Successful local injected callback and validation rejection cases
Callback mutation isolation and exception handling
File CLI, stdin CLI, missing-file errors and invalid-input errors

bounded_working_scope.scope: Local, in-memory analysis of supplied explicit string-valued assertions with literal source excerpts.
limitations: No automatic extraction of claims from raw prose.
Lexical excerpt checks do not establish semantic entailment, truth, negation scope or source authenticity.
Lexical retrieval can miss paraphrases or retrieve irrelevant term matches; it does not verify full question coverage.
No semantic synonym, entity, unit, timestamp or context resolution.
Differing values can represent different circumstances rather than true contradictions.
Different document IDs do not establish independent authorship or independent evidence.
No confidence calibration, external fact-checking, browsing, persistence, concurrency or access-control implementation.
No resource quotas, large-corpus benchmark, adversarial fuzzing or production hardening is claimed.
Arbitrary free-form LLM prose is intentionally not accepted because structural citation validation cannot prove it supported.
Callback validation is tested using local deterministic fakes, not a real LLM.
bounded_working_scope.statement: This build demonstrates only the implemented and locally tested working scope. It is not production-certified and carries no production guarantee.
